newsitem.title: CHINA: Pioneer Tibet share welcome as "minority concept".
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Tibet share welcome as "minority concept".

text.p: Investors are expected to warmly welcome Tibet's first-ever industrial company to list on the Shanghai bourse, brokers said on Thursday.
Tibet Shengdi (Holy Land) Company Ltd said in the China Securities newspaper on Thursday it would soon issue 15 million A shares at four yuan ($0.5) each.
The company, which produces mineral water and operates a hotel in the Tibetan capital Lhasa, will be the first industrial firm to issue shares from Tibet, the poorest part of China, it said.
Analysts said investors believed share issues from minority regions of China such as Tibet would receive preferential support from the central government, making them good targets for speculation.

"Investors are still keen on the minority share concept," said one broker with Guotai Securities. "Previous issues from minority areas have done well. The company makes mineral water in an area with very little pollution."

Over 90 percent of China's 1.2 billion people are of Han race. The rest of the country is made up of more than 50 minorities who mainly live in economically undeveloped regions in China's centre, west and south.

Only a few companies from these minority areas have listed shares in stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen, which are largely dominated by shares from companies in the richer east and south. But the "minority" shares have performed well.

Only one other Tibetan company, Tibet Pearl Star Co, a hotel group, has listed shares. It listed A shares in Shanghai in February 1995 but most of its assets are in the southwest province of Sichuan and not in Tibet.
A second Chinese broker was also bullish on the stock.
"The issue price is cheap, at four yuan," he said.

"The central government has promised to make development in the west a priority in the ninth Five-Year Plan (1996-2000) and will support projects in areas like Tibet. I expect a good reception from the market."
"Holy Land has a good product in mineral water," he said. "If it was making refrigerators, then few people would buy it. Our water in Shanghai is polluted. We need good mineral water."

In the first half of 1996, Holy Land posted profits of 2.23 million yuan, the same as for all of 1995, on sales of 9.74 million yuan, against 14.45 million in all of 1995, said an official at the company's underwriter, the Trust and Investment Company of the China People's Insurance Company.
The firm, which has 310 workers, has annual output of 10,000 tonnes of "Himalayan Mineral Water", some of it transported by air to parts of China other than Tibet, she said.
The money raised from the listing will be used to remodel its hotel in Lhasa and buy additional production equipment.
"We are very confident about the listing," she said. "Supply of new shares in China cannot meet demand. The share price is very cheap. Investors welcome minority shares," she said.
"The quality of water in Tibet is very high," she added.
Tibet is China's most economically depressed region, due partly to poor transport links with China's richer areas.
